content.title: What are Annotations?
content.description: Annotations are metadata added to Java code that provide additional information to the compiler, JVM, or frameworks. They do not directly change program logic but influence how the code is processed.

content.content: Annotations were introduced in Java 5 to allow developers to attach metadata to classes, methods, fields, constructors, parameters, and other program elements. They help improve code readability, enable compile-time checking, generate code automatically, and are heavily used in frameworks like Spring, Hibernate, and JUnit.

content.title: Why Use Annotations?
content.content: Annotations reduce boilerplate code, improve maintainability, enable framework features, and provide useful information to the compiler and runtime.
Java provides several built-in annotations that assist the compiler and improve code quality.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Annotations provide metadata—they describe the code rather than directly executing program logic.

content.content: The @Override annotation tells the compiler that a method is intended to override a superclass method. If the method signature is incorrect, the compiler reports an error.

content.title: @Override Example

content.content: The @Deprecated annotation indicates that a class, method, or field should no longer be used because a better alternative exists.
The @SuppressWarnings annotation suppresses specific compiler warnings when the developer intentionally wants to ignore them.
The @FunctionalInterface annotation ensures that an interface contains exactly one abstract method, making it suitable for lambda expressions.

content.title: @FunctionalInterface Example

content.content: Developers can create their own annotations to provide metadata specific to their applications or frameworks.
Retention policies determine how long annotation information is available.

content.title: Sticky Notes on Documents
content.content: Imagine attaching sticky notes to important documents. The notes don't change the document's content but provide instructions or additional information for people reading it. Annotations work the same way by attaching metadata to Java code.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Annotations, @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings, @FunctionalInterface, custom annotations, retention policies, target elements, reflection, and annotation processing are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Do annotations execute business logic?
items.answer: No. They only provide metadata that is interpreted by the compiler, JVM, or frameworks.

items.question: Can @Override be applied to any method?
items.answer: No. It should only be used for methods that actually override a superclass or interface method.

items.question: Are custom annotations automatically processed?
items.answer: No. They require annotation processors or reflection to be useful.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Annotations provide metadata to Java code, helping the compiler, JVM, and frameworks perform additional processing without changing the program's core logic.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Annotations are metadata for Java code.
They improve readability and reduce boilerplate.
Custom annotations are widely used in frameworks like Spring and Hibernate.
